ceiling_directive: Prove unrestricted single-edge transfer for profile-changing additions, including SCC-merging arrows, first cross-SCC bidirected connections, and bidirected loops, thereby establishing unrestricted union closure and in-class greatestness.
improvement_directive: Complete the contextual-replacement theorem for every edge appearing in an E-equivalent graph, explicitly handling collider activation and SCC-tail changes. Then use the proved equivalence to upgrade the union candidate and simultaneous admissible-edge construction to unconditional unrestricted results.
critique: The note proves a greatest representative only inside a graph-dependent fixed mixed-SCC-profile family; it does not prove the advertised unrestricted greatest-representative result for finite directed mixed graphs. Profile-changing edges—especially SCC-merging arrows, first bidirected connections between SCC rectangles, and bidirected loops—remain outside the transfer and saturation theorems, so unrestricted union closure, in-class status of the oracle union, and the compelled-edge deletion shortcut are still open or conditional. The fixed-profile saturation is a genuine but narrow replacement result, while singleton-oracle recovery of the raw union and intersection is largely finite exhaustive enumeration and supplies neither an efficient discovery method nor the missing structural interpretation. The directed-subclass reduction also relies on a published greatest-element lemma without an exact theorem-number citation or statement-level source verification, and the package remains below a leading-journal contribution because its central all-DMG conjecture is unresolved. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
